Question B-006-011-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Adding directors and using a longer boom lets a Yagi concentrate more energy in the forward lobe, so forward gain increases.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Front-to-back ratio increases": Front-to-back ratio can be affected by tuning and reflector design, but adding directors and boom length is primarily a way to increase forward gain.
- sourceIndex 2: "Beamwidth increases": As a Yagi gains directivity, the main lobe generally becomes narrower. Increased beamwidth is the opposite of the usual higher-gain effect.
- sourceIndex 3: "Power handling capability increases": Power handling depends on conductor size, traps, insulators, and matching hardware. More directors on a boom do not automatically raise the safe transmitter power.
